title: Composable Device-Independent Quantum Digital Signatures
authors: Jing-Wei Bian, Bing-Hong Li, Xu-Yang Lu, Shi-Gen Li, Hua-Lei Yin, Zeng-Bing Chen
abstract: Extending device-independent (DI) quantum cryptography to composably support all fundamental information security objectives is crucial for secure quantum networks. Achieving this goal requires composable quantum digital signatures (QDSs), which support integrity, authenticity, and nonrepudiation when integrated into quantum networks. Yet existing QDS protocols generally rely on assumptions about the underlying quantum devices, while their security analyses remain largely restricted to stand-alone settings, leaving related-key attacks on the underlying linear feedback shift register (LFSR)-based Toeplitz authentication unaddressed. Here, we establish the first composable security framework for QDS within constructive cryptography, and realize the corresponding ideal QDS resource by developing a DI-QDS protocol employing one-time universal hashing and multi-channel multiplexing. We further derive a related-key security bound for the underlying LFSR-based Toeplitz authentication, thereby establishing unforgeability while extending the forgery boundary considered in previous QDS security analyses. We also demonstrate the practical feasibility of our DI-QDS protocol under realistic quantum network conditions in the finite-size regime, with numerical simulations showing that it enables efficient signing of multibit documents over metropolitan-scale distances. Our results establish QDS as a composable cryptographic primitive and extend DI quantum cryptography to support the full range of information security objectives with composable security guarantees in future quantum networks.
summary: This paper develops a novel, composably secure framework for Quantum Digital Signatures (QDS) that operates in a device-independent manner. It achieves this by proposing a DI-QDS protocol utilizing one-time universal hashing and multi-channel multiplexing. The work is significant for establishing QDS as a robust, composable primitive for future quantum networks.
main_problem: The paper addresses the need to extend device-independent (DI) quantum cryptography to composably support all fundamental information security objectives, specifically requiring composable quantum digital signatures (QDSs).
main_result: The authors establish the first composable security framework for QDS and realize an ideal DI-QDS resource using one-time universal hashing and multi-channel multiplexing.
method: The methodology involves establishing a composable security framework, developing a DI-QDS protocol, and deriving a related-key security bound for the underlying Toeplitz authentication.
model_or_system: The protocol utilizes an all-photon DI-Key Generation Protocol (DI-KGP) involving three parties (Alice, Bob, Charlie) and relies on entanglement distribution via QND measurements at an intermediate node (Eve).
key_observables: Successful Bell measurement clicks, CHSH inequality violation ($\sum \chi(U_j = 0) \le n_r \gamma (1 - \omega_{thr})$), and the final signature $	ext{Sig}$.
important_parameters: The protocol is demonstrated to work in the finite-size regime over lossy quantum channels, enabling signing over metropolitan-scale distances.
main_assumptions: The security analysis requires avoiding memory loopholes by setting up independent sublaboratories/devices for each party.
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically illustrates the distribution stage involving Alice, Bob, Eve, PBSs, HWPs, and BSA measurements for entanglement distribution.
paper_structure: The paper details the DI-KGP distribution stage, followed by the QDS messaging stage which uses an OTUH-QDS scheme based on LFSR-based Toeplitz matrices for signing and verification.
why_interesting: The focus on composable security and extending DI quantum cryptography to support full information security objectives is highly relevant to the theoretical understanding of quantum network protocols.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Schematic of the distribution stage of the proposed QDS protocol. (a) Alice and Bob each generate mr entangled photon pairs. For each pair, the local k photon is measured immediately, while the corresponding t photon is transmitted to the intermediate node Eve through an optical channel. At Eve’s node, quantum nondemolition (QND) measurements identify the successfully arrived photons. Based on the QND outcomes, SWs adaptively pair the arrived photons from Alice and Bob and route each formed photon pair to a separate BSA, where the Bell measurements are performed in parallel. (b) Optical implementation of one BSA, consisting of polarizing beam splitters (PBSs), half-wave plates...

FIG. 2. Schematic of the messaging stage of the proposed QDS protocol following successful slot preparation. The pro- cess involves three stages: the signing of Alice, the verifica- tion of Bob, and the verificationof Charlie. Information is ex- changed among three parties via classical and authenticated classical communication channels.
